text:
maria: Quick sync — saw canary show a small p99 latency hump when long-seq tenants interleave with many short requests. Trace looks like batch assembly churn + KV-miss waits causing kernel-selection thrash. Trying a 'credit dampening' heuristic to reduce short-seq capture. Anyone else notice this?

sam: saw ~3% p99 bump in last deploy window, initially blamed kernel swap. digging into traces looks like repeated small batches forcing kernel reselects and cold KV lookups.

raj: attached quick profile dump from canary run (trimmed):
```
batch_formation_cpu: 46%
avg_batch_len: 7
avg_short_seq_len: 8
avg_long_seq_len: 128
kv_miss_wait_ms: p50=4.2 p95=18.1 p99=42.7
token_budget_rebalance_spikes: 03:12:42, 03:25:04
kernel_switches: 1.8k/hr during spike
```

ella: sounds like two things: 1) our batcher aggressively prefers filling with short sequences, 2) token budget refill policy aggressively credits lanes that just finished which amplifies the short/long feedback loop. propose a dampening multiplier for short lanes and a minimum reserve for long lanes.

maria: suggested heuristic prototype (runtime flags):
```
short_dampening_multiplier = 0.35  # multiply new credits given to short lanes
long_reserved_tokens = 64          # tokens reserved per long sequence tenant
refill_interval_ms = 25           # how often token pool is refilled
min_batch_len_for_kernel_stability = 12
```

sam: question — if long_reserved_tokens are held but long tenant has high KV-hit rate (so lower compute), are we wasting capacity? or do we rely on runtime to shrink batch sizes dynamically?

raj: good call. idea: make reserve adaptive based on kv_hit_ratio. offline rule: reserve = base_reserve * (1 - kv_hit_ratio). so high kv-hit lowers the reserve. also publish a hit_bias metric per tenant.

kim: to action this we need metrics: denied_credit_reasons (enum), avg_batch_len_by_seqlen_bucket, kv_hit_ratio_by_tenant, kernel_switch_count. can we get these in prometheus?

ella: I'll add probes in the batcher and KV layer. names: `inference.batcher.denied_credit_reasons`, `inference.batch.avg_len.bucketed`, `inference.kv.hit_ratio_tenant`. also add a tag for kernel_id on batch emit.

devops-bot: deploy/canary job #4372 succeeded — canary config: credit-dampening-experiment v2 deployed to zone-a (link: https://ci.internal/job/4372) :white_check_mark:

maria: plan: run 2h canary with controlled mix (30% long, 70% short) and collect p50/p95/p99, kernel-selection counts, kv hit distribution, denied_credit_reasons. baseline vs v2.

sam: will seed loadgen with the mix and pin model 7B-quant on lane-A to isolate kernel-selection noise.

raj: add safety fallback: if denied_credit_reasons.type=="starve_long" > 5% over a 5m window, trigger fallback to round-robin preemptive admission and disable dampening for 10m.

ella: noted — PR: https://repo/infra/pull/1427 (config + metrics) :thumbsup:

maria: awesome. schedule a quick sync after 2h to decide whether to roll forward or iterate. thanks all :eyes:
